newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says Israel bourse will rise again.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says Israel bourse will rise again.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that the Israeli stock market would rise once it realised how serious the government was in its intentions on privatisation and budget cuts.

"It has happened many times in past that the bourse has made mistakes in its estimates. It is mistaken now in the fact that it does not estimate correctly the seriousness of our budget intentions and the intentions of our privatisation and reform plans," Netanyahu said in an interview with the daily Haaretz.

"What will happen is that instead of bourse rises preceding the privatisations, the privatisations will precede the rises in the stock exchange, and only after it will become clear how much this trend is serious and consistent, will the appropriate reaction in the bourse happen."

Netanyahu said he had set up a committee to study claims by the central bank that the government had deviated from the 1996 budget deficit target of 7.6 billion shekels by about four billion shekels, against Treasury figures that there was a deviation of three billion shekels. "If there is such a deviation, then we will act immediately to return to the original government decision," he said.

Referring to the government's sale of Bank Hapoalim and the fact that the main group of investors led by Claridge Israel had pulled out of the bid, Netanyahu said that it is possible that a sale of Bank Hapoalim as a whole was "too big a package and difficult to digest."
He said he was considering the possibility of splitting up the bank's holdings and selling it off in smaller parts. "There is an interest in investor groups in some parts of the bank."
